title: DoDonPachi DaiOuJou (Black Label)
blurb: Vertical shooter on IGS PGM hardware, translated from the Version-B program rather than CPU-emulated. Stage 1 is feature-complete with live enemies, weapons, boss, result screen, HUD, chaining, hypers, rank, sound, music and replay. Stage 2 boots and scrolls; its background and first ten chronological enemy families are ported, covering 323 of 332 spawn records at W179.

rom.note: A MAME set, not a single file. The cartridge holds TWO COMPLETE GAMES and the boot menu defaults to VERSION-A (2002.04.05 MASTER VER) after ~5 s; this port targets VERSION-B (2002.10.07 BLACK VER), the $23xxxx-$28xxxx build. An address in the $13xxxx/$14xxxx range is a defect unless a comment says why -- except the interrupt handlers, which really are build A's on a VERSION-B run (measured three ways, 02-review.md).

screen.note: The cabinet is TATE. MAME's visible area is 448x224 and the port renders that, then rotates CCW for the canvas -- src/render/index.js rotateCCW(), the same rotation tools/framerender.py's np.rot90 performs, so the browser and the gate PNGs show the same picture the right way up.

display.frameHzNote: 15625/264 Hz EXACTLY, a set_raw derivation from pixclock 10 MHz / (640 x 264). Frame period exactly 16.896 ms; 337,920 68000 cycles per frame at 20 MHz. Confirmed from -listxml and from the running machine to the attosecond. DERIVED, not rounded -- and emphatically not the '~54 fps' of the first conversation. src/machine.js MACHINE.refreshHz is the same number computed rather than typed, and src/web/app.js refuses to boot if the two disagree.

code.pageNote: code.page, NOT code.entry. The root launcher expects a generic inline boot contract, while this translated PGM main loop owns a dedicated TATE host, asset loader, frame cadence, Web Audio runtime, and REC/PLAY UI. The picker therefore links to its own page.

input.note: Bit POSITIONS in the P1 input mirror $803970, which is derived from the raw 68000 port word $C08000 by build A's $13D464 (one read per IRQ6, measured). The port takes the RAW PORT WORD as its input so the mirrors stay a genuinely compared field; src/input.js portWordFromBits() is the inverse, checked against the board: 1P Start alone -> $FFFE, P1 Button 3 held -> $FF7F. src/machine.js BIT is the authority and tests/web-input.test.js holds this table, BIT and src/web/input.js against each other.
input.keymapNote: Matched on e.code, i.e. PHYSICAL key position. KeyZ and KeyY are BOTH shot: on a Swiss QWERTZ keyboard the key printed Z sits where QWERTY has Y and reports KeyY. A standing requirement, asked for twice.

touchLayout.note: The on-screen pad in index.html. The d-pad is ONE pointer-capture surface hit-tested as a 3x3 grid, not four buttons: four captured buttons can never report a diagonal, because the capture that stops a stuck direction is also what stops a second button ever seeing the finger. A vertical shooter without diagonals is not playable. The corner cells report TWO bits, which is exactly what $803970 carries -- one bit per direction, tested independently by the mover at $141B2E. The face cluster is stacked, START above the three fire buttons: inline, the row is wider than the space beside the d-pad and the rightmost button falls off a narrow phone.

assets.note: ROM-derived and gitignored, like every other game here. BG and TX tiles are decoded to one byte per pixel and sprite streams are rebased into deferred shards. The board capture remains reference and seed material for state not yet translated; port-generated sprites are the default live source. tools/bundlegate.mjs renders the demo from the exported bundle and must remain 15955968/15955968 pixels against MAME.
